SPDX/module docs identify build_manifest as operation-to-candidate metadata center. Imports feature flags/read-write gates, overlay/types, CommitHandler plus manifest readers, row-ID/version helpers, FRI gate/recognizers, MemWAL helpers, UpdateMode, preparation/validation/update-map functions, operation payloads, key metadata names, truthy parser, exact file versions, object store/path, Roaring, ordered/hash collections, Arc and UUID. Imported commit/manifest IO powers restoration; main candidate building is synchronous.

Public RANGE_SEGMENTS_CONFIG_KEY is exactly lance.row_ids.range_segments. Docs say opt-in converts bitmap row-ID segments to a compact in-memory Ranges form serialized as existing Range records; older readers may be slow, and turning off only stops new conversions. Private range_segments_enabled looks in manifest.config and uses str_is_truthy directly: missing/unrecognized false, recognized case-insensitive spellings true, no whitespace trim (rust/lance-core/src/utils/parse.rs:5-11). This is persisted config, not an environment setting.

Private apply_range_segments returns Ok immediately unless destination manifest enables conversion. If current manifest also enables it, build HashMap fragment ID to starting raw byte pointer for only inline row-ID entries; otherwise empty. Duplicate IDs overwrite earlier pointer entries. Equality later is ID plus pointer, not encoded-content digest or bytes. Raw pointers are compared, never dereferenced; no unsafe block.

Arc::make_mut detaches fragment vector when shared, then visit each inline row-ID sequence. Same ID/start pointer in enabled current manifest skips decode; other inline entries decode fallibly, run use_range_segments and replace bytes only when it reports change. Column/missing metadata skipped. Decoder errors can follow earlier local fragment changes; no rollback within helper. New allocation with equal bytes is decoded; pointer equality assumes valid unmodified shared backing. Enabling on a previously disabled table attempts every inline fragment. No storage IO.

Transaction::fragments_with_ids is pub(super), generic IntoIterator<Item=Fragment> with returned lazy iterator borrowing mutable u64 counter for lifetime a. Each consumed fragment with id0 gets current counter then ordinary increment; nonzero IDs pass unchanged without advancing/reserving counter. Allocation happens on iteration, not method call. No collision/u32-limit/overflow validation; valid externally assigned IDs and counter state are caller responsibilities. Counter0 can assign legitimate0 and still advance.

Private data_storage_format_from_files takes fragments and optional exact request. Explicit V1 first infers homogeneous existing file version and errors if it is non-V1; inference errors propagate. Explicit non-V1 wins without inference, allowing mixed prewritten versions for later finalization. No request uses inferred version. None after empty-file inference becomes DataStorageFormat::default. This chooses default metadata, not actual file conversion or complete final file-version validation.

Public async Transaction::restore_old_manifest borrows store/CommitHandler/base/config/current and accepts target version/tx path; returns owned Manifest and index Vec. Await version location, await manifest read, then require both read and write capability before mutating metadata or reading indices. Set supplied timestamp/transaction path, await index read, then validate tagged paired flags. IO/errors propagate in this order; cancellation can drop awaits/local candidate, with no write/publication performed here.

Restore raises target max_fragment_id and next_row_id to maxima with current high-water marks. Rejects current stable-ID table restored to target without stable IDs, with target version/context: reverting to physical-address identity could collide with allocated IDs. Then inherit sticky feature flags and return. Target manifest version itself is not incremented here, and contents/config/index entries remain restored state apart from listed metadata changes. No data-file existence/rewrite/cleanup checks here.

Public logical_index_segments filters system indices using exact reserved-name predicate, groups all other physical segments by owned name in BTreeMap, clones UUID plus Option bitmap into CoverageIdentity, then unstable-sorts each Vec by UUID only. Order-independent equality assumes unique segment UUIDs; duplicates with different bitmaps can retain differing tie order because tie key excludes bitmap. Duplicate entries are not removed. No file/detail/version/timestamp comparison; allocations include names, vectors and cloned bitmaps.

Public apply_mem_wal_index_coverage mutates final index slice from prior logical-segment snapshot, optional original read-version manifest/indices and new version. Docs derive credit from covering all fragments live at original read_version, capped by current compacted progress; merely reported claims could become stale on rebase. Missing catchup is documented differently in required-coverage versus legacy read modes. This method signature has no explicit coverage-mode flag and its actual early returns follow below; global reader policy requires separate analysis.

Find first final index named __lance_mem_wal; absence returns Ok. Decode a clone; only if both compacted_sstables and index_catchup are empty return unchanged. Compute logical segments after and take catchup vector out of local decoded details. Missing/invalid Any errors before any caller mutation. This branch does not directly inspect a feature flag or maintain_all_indexes. Duplicate reserved entries ignored after first.

Optional read-version state searches its first reserved-name entry, clones/decodes with Option/Result transpose, and propagates malformed details even when credit might ultimately be absent. Build one tuple per current compacted marker in its order: shard UUID,current generation,min(first read marker generation or0,current). Current duplicate shard markers stay duplicated. Read state missing or missing shard contributes0. Capping by current protects against credit from a subsequently rolled-back compaction; no monotonic-state validation performed.

Build optional RoaringBitmap of every read-manifest fragment ID cast unchecked u64->u32. covers_read_version returns false if no read state or empty required set, explicitly refusing vacuous credit because historical UpdateMemWalState could omit fragments while SSTables remain sole data copy. Otherwise union every physical segment bitmap; any None returns false even if other segments already cover all required IDs. Return required subset of union. No row counts, deletion vectors, field identity or per-generation fragment mapping is checked.

For each after logical index in BTreeMap name order, unchanged means full CoverageIdentity Vec equals segments_before[name], including bitmap and Option shape. Only unchanged names may carry first matching prior catchup entry. Independently recompute proof of read-version coverage. If neither carried nor proven, omit name. Changed UUID or in-place bitmap narrowing can remove credit; additional outer metadata fields do not affect equality. Prior duplicate name entries beyond first are not merged.

For each current compacted shard tuple, prior generation is first carried shard match or0; new credit is capped read generation only when proven, else0. Emit min(max(prior,credited),committed). This keeps higher prior credit on unchanged index while clamping rollback and never credits post-read generations. Emit all current shard tuples including zeros if any generation positive; omit the entire name if all zero, also true for no shards. Explicitly sort rebuilt names, though BTreeMap traversal already sorted them. No removal of duplicate shard tuples.

Sort old catchup entries by name and compare to rebuilt with order-sensitive nested Vec equality. Equal returns without touching final metadata, preserving UUID and actual prior byte ordering even if only names had been unsorted. Otherwise find old names absent from rebuilt (nested scans, duplicates may log repeatedly), info-log dropped names, store rebuilt details and replace selected slot through fresh metadata constructor. Errors before assignment leave caller slice unchanged; info log can precede constructor error. Successful replacement changes UUID/timestamp and constructor outer defaults as documented in mem_wal.rs598-618; no physical file IO.

Public withdraw_coverage_invalidated_after_build accepts changed logical names and candidate version. Empty names or absent reserved MemWAL entry returns Ok. Decode copy, retain catchup names not contained in changed slice, return unchanged if no entry removed. Otherwise log the complete supplied changed list and replace same index slot with newly encoded metadata. It only removes credit, never derives new credit; duplicates/missing names harmless, contains scans give O(catchup*changed) comparisons. Failure before replacement preserves caller slice. Docs identify post-build migrate_indices bitmap recalculation as caller rationale, full caller still pending.
